questions.stem: The Clifford Constitution of 1922 is best remembered for

options.text: introducing the elective principle, with four elected seats in Lagos and Calabar
making Nigeria a republic with an executive President

questions.explanation: Clifford allowed three elected members for Lagos and one for Calabar in a Legislative Council that covered the South only. The North was excluded. That tiny franchise was enough to produce Herbert Macaulay's NNDP. Federal states, an executive presidency and the AU belong to much later history.

distractorRationale.c: The executive presidency arrived with the 1979 Constitution

questions.stem: The constitution that introduced a true federal system in Nigeria, with exclusive and concurrent lists and regional premiers, was the
questions.explanation: Lyttleton 1954 divided powers by legislative lists, left residual matters to the regions, created the office of regional premier, and made Lagos a federal territory. Richards had begun regionalism but had not yet produced a full federation. Clifford had no regions in that sense. The 1999 Constitution is a later federal document, not the first.

distractorRationale.a: Clifford created a Southern Legislative Council with four elected seats, not a federation
distractorRationale.b: Richards introduced regional councils and brought the North into the centre, but stopped short of full federalism
distractorRationale.d: 1999 continues federalism; it did not introduce it

questions.stem: Nigeria's four republics are conventionally dated
questions.explanation: The First Republic began with the 1963 Republican Constitution, the Second with the 1979 presidential constitution, the Third was aborted after the 12 June 1993 election, and the Fourth began on 29 May 1999. 1914–1954 are colonial dates; 1966 and later military years are interruptions, not republics; 1976–1996 are state-creation dates.

distractorRationale.a: Those are colonial constitution years, not republics
distractorRationale.c: 1960 is independence (still under the Queen); 1966, 1975 and 1985 are associated with military rule
distractorRationale.d: Those years mark expansions in the number of states

questions.stem: The Third Republic is described as aborted because

options.text: no election was ever held in 1993
the 12 June 1993 presidential election was annulled and civilian rule was not allowed to take office
Nigeria left the United Nations in 1993
the 1999 Constitution abolished all political parties

questions.explanation: Under Babangida's two-party transition, Nigerians voted on 12 June 1993. The result, widely credited to M.K.O. Abiola of the SDP, was annulled. The civilian structures of the Third Republic therefore never fully took power. An Interim National Government followed, then Abacha's coup. That is why textbooks speak of an aborted Third Republic.

distractorRationale.a: The election was held; the problem was the annulment, not the absence of a poll
distractorRationale.c: Nigeria did not leave the UN in 1993
distractorRationale.d: The 1999 Constitution restored multi-party civilian rule rather than abolishing parties

questions.stem: A persistent problem of Nigerian federalism is

options.text: the absence of any state governments
disputes over revenue allocation and the fears of minority groups
Nigeria's membership of a confederation with Ghana
the lack of a written constitution

questions.explanation: Who gets what share of oil and other federally collected revenue, and how smaller ethnic groups are protected against domination, have driven state creation, derivation arguments and agitation since the 1950s. Nigeria has states, is not in a confederation with Ghana, and has a written constitution.

distractorRationale.a: Nigeria has 36 states and the FCT
distractorRationale.c: Nigeria is a federation of its own units, not a confederation with Ghana
distractorRationale.d: The 1999 Constitution is a written, codified document

questions.stem: General Yakubu Gowon created twelve states in 1967, replacing the old regional structure during the crisis that became the civil war.
questions.explanation: True. On 27 May 1967 Gowon replaced the four regions with twelve states. The move aimed to undercut secession and to answer minority fears. Later military governments raised the number to 19, 21, 30 and then 36 (1996), which is the structure the 1999 Constitution inherited.

distractorRationale.b: The twelve-state structure of 1967 is a standard landmark on the federalism timeline
